court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: 8th Joint Civil Judge (Senior Division), Aurangabad, HMP No.66/2024
case_name: Ganesh Ashok Sabale vs Vaishnavi W/O Ganesh Sabale
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent married in 2022, but started living separately in 2022 due to matrimonial dispute. They filed for divorce by mutual consent under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court rejected their application to waive the 6-month cooling period.

legal_principles.principle: The statutory period of six months specified in Section 13B (2) is not mandatory but directory.

legal_principles.principle: The Court can exercise its discretion in the facts and circumstances of each case where there is no possibility of parties resuming cohabitation and there are chances of alternative rehabilitation.
legal_principles.held: Since we are of the view that the period mentioned in Section 13B (2) is not mandatory but directory, it will be open to the Court to exercise its discretion in the facts and circumstances of each case where there is no possibility of parties resuming cohabitation and there are chances of alternative rehabilitation.
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh Vs. Harveen Kaur, (2017) 8 SCC 746

legal_principles.principle: All efforts for mediation / conciliation including efforts in terms of Order XXXIIA Rule 3 Code of Civil Procedure / Section 23 (2) of the Act / Section 9 of the Family Courts Act to reunite the parties have failed and there is no likelihood of success in that direction by any further efforts.

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is allowed and the order dated 22.02.2024 passed by the trial court is set aside.
